column1: # The anchor of the slot matrix (@PLN221): what each slot's PLAIN statement must leave
# Columns, tab-separated: slot id, collection kind or `*`, the changed fields.
#   fields  the `name=value` fields of the cell's final line that differ from the untouched
#           world, parted by ` ; `, each with its new value exactly as printed; `-` when the
#           statement must change nothing.  Every other field must stay as it was.
# The world (scripts/syntax_slots_prelude.loft): i=1, j=3, b=true, nb=false, x="abc",
# fl=1.5, en=Green; vi=[10,20,30,40]; xs holds P{1,"a"} P{2,"b"} P{3,"c"}; r and h.ws[0] are
# W{n:1, t:"abc", …, items: those three}; h.ws[1] is W{n:2, t:"y", …, items:[P{4,"d"}]}.  A
# collection is shown as `length:` and one letter per lookup 0..9 — by position for a
# vector, by key for the keyed kinds.
# EVERY VALUE HERE IS COMPUTED BY HAND from the statement and the rules.  `slot_matrix.py
# expect --propose` prints what the compiler answers for a slot that has no row; that is a
# proposal to check, never the expectation.  Each plain cell is compared with its row on
# every run; a slot without a row is named by `slot_matrix.py expect`.
